## TL;DR

This CLI usability pass corrected two invalid-input cases that could otherwise look successful: an unknown `list` status previously acted like an unfiltered board request, and invalid `upgrade --channel` input could silently fall back to stable. A follow-up review found that repeated `--channel` options validated only the first value; the command now rejects repeats with next-step guidance. The branch includes focused regression tests and a scratch-repository QA findings document. No mutating command was run against the real board.

## Work and rationale

I resumed the existing task worktree after its second review. The latest review report identified one bug: `repoos upgrade --channel beta --channel invalid` validated beta, ignored the later option, and proceeded. I inspected `cmdUpgrade` and the upgrade tests in this worktree. The current implementation first gathers every `--channel` occurrence and rejects more than one before install-kind detection or any release work. The error tells the user to use the flag once and lists the supported channels. The test calls the command with the reported beta-then-invalid sequence and asserts a nonzero exit code and both actionable error lines.

The review also confirms the earlier help finding is fixed. The `list` help entry now includes `archived`, matching the status accepted by the handler, and its test checks the visible usage. The implementation also validates unknown list statuses before server or local board lookup, showing the supported status choices and usage before returning a failure.

The CLI QA findings document records the original probe method and boundaries. It covers `--help` for each requested command, missing required arguments for representative task commands, an invalid restart port, unknown list status, invalid/missing upgrade channels, and the repeated-channel review case. Probes were run against a disposable scratch repository using the compiled CLI entry point. No successful task mutation was performed, and no real board mutation occurred. The report distinguishes these cases from valid-ID server-backed actions that require a running control plane.

## Approaches tried

I read both stored review reports and traced each finding to the current branch and tests. The first report described an omitted `archived` option; direct inspection showed the current help and test already cover it, so I retained that fix. For the latest finding, I verified that validation is done before install detection, which ensures invalid input fails consistently for source, package-manager, and standalone installs. I kept the existing early-return style so the validation path cannot continue into release lookup or update behavior.

The original CLI QA used a disposable repository and the worktree's compiled CLI rather than invoking a linked executable against the main checkout. One initial read-only exploration printed the main board before the scratch setup was complete; it did not mutate anything. Subsequent probes used the scratch setup, and the findings explicitly document this limitation and the lack of server-backed valid-ID coverage.

## Challenges and blockers

This task resumed with prior implementation already present, so the first challenge was separating current state from old review conclusions. The first report concerned an earlier tree and was already addressed by the branch. The second report was actionable and specific, and its code path and test are now present in the worktree.

The scratch QA did not start a server or exercise successful `start`, `done`, `review`, or `handoff-status` requests with valid IDs. Those responses depend on live server state; the findings do not claim them as verified. The acceptance work here is focused on command help and representative invalid-input behavior, and the limitations are stated in the QA document.

## Key learnings

Enum-like arguments should be rejected at the CLI boundary before side effects or I/O, and errors should show valid choices plus a usable command form. Repeated options need an explicit policy: silently honoring only the first can hide a typo in a later value. Validating the entire option occurrence set before selecting a value prevents that class of error. Help text and accepted values should also share regression coverage so additions such as `archived` stay discoverable.

When resuming a reviewed branch, stored reports must be checked against the actual current implementation and tests. Here, that avoided duplicating a completed help fix while ensuring the newest parser bug was covered. The scoped RepoOS check is the final correctness gate requested for this handoff; RepoOS will perform its own verification during handoff and close-out.
